concerns.text: Tasks T008b and T026c implement 'domain-stratified analysis' (separate tests per domain) as a fallback or alternative to the Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM). FR-005 and Constitution Principle VI explicitly mandate LMM with 'Domain' as a random intercept, with fallback only to paired t-tests/Wilcoxon if LMM is infeasible. Replacing the primary LMM requirement with a stratified analysis constitutes a semantic weakening of the statistical methodology required by the spec.

Task T014a specifies loading a 'frozen DistilBERT intent classifier' but does not explicitly mandate the 'CPU-only' constraint in the task description's acceptance criteria, only in the parenthetical note. FR-002 and the Constitution Principle VII require the system to be 'CPU-tractable' and run on a 'CPU-only runner'. While the note exists, the task's explicit acceptance criteria should enforce the 'no CUDA' and 'memory < 2GB' constraints as a hard gate to prevent silent relaxation of the resource constraints.

Task T029 specifies outputting 'data/samples/failure_cases.json' with a fixed seed. However, FR-007 requires the system to output a 'simple random sample of failure cases (stratified by domain if N > 50)'. The task description mentions 'stratified by domain' in the text but does not explicitly include the 'if N > 50' condition in the implementation logic description, risking a deviation from the spec's conditional stratification rule.
